key_findings_by_avenue.1_caucasus: All 5 Az/Geo/Am popular-history Hagigi MS locations map onto existing current poetry-witness register entries (bl_or_9493, suleymaniye_fatih_3808, matenadaran_965, tehran_university_8198). manuscript.az 'newly acquired from Süleymaniye' is a copy/microfilm of Fatih 3808. manuscript.ge LIVE under direct-route (was ECONNREFUSED under alternate-route); test-mode operation; Persian Afshar-period scope (EAP1526) confirms post-Cihanşah holdings only. Matenadaran has no online search.
key_findings_by_avenue.4_south_asia: All 6 portals EXHAUSTED-NEGATIVE or BLOCKED. 8 of 14 grepped printed catalogues delivered strong negatives with healthy OCR (Bankipore Persian Vols II/III/XIII via Khuda Bakhsh, Ivanow 1924 + Mirza Ashraf Ali via Asiatic Society Kolkata). Bonus future scope chancery finding: Bodleian MS Pers d. 84 (Vol III entry 2711) is an insha collection containing one Cihansah firman to Sultan Muhammad II ~1455. Residual gaps: Salar Jung Vol IV (highest-yield window, 500MB PDF not retrieved); NAMAMI/Kriti Sampada (Indian-IP needed).
key_findings_by_avenue.2_3_central_asia_russia_yerevan: All 8 portals EXHAUSTED-NEGATIVE via web. Major triangulation finding: Az Wikipedia 'NYC Gazaryan -> Yerevan University -> Hüseynzade publication' narrative CONFLATES BL Or 9493's London examination with the Yerevan-held codex. Hüseyinzadə was at Yerevan Pedagogical Institute (NOT YSU); discovery 1961; first publication Yerevan 1966. Gazaryan-bequest codex is most plausibly Matenadaran MS 965 itself, via 1959 YSU-to-Matenadaran institutional consolidation per Iranica MATENADARAN. Bonus future scope chancery lead: Kostikyan Persian Decrees vols III (2005) + IV (2008) parallel to asnad.org. Tatar/Kazan/Bashkort portals all unresolvable/defunct.
key_findings_by_avenue.5_6_provincial_ottoman_sufi: All 4 site-restricted Google sweeps returned ZERO Cihanşah / Hakîkî / Karakoyunlu hits on yazmalar.gov.tr, katalog.isam.org.tr, mkutup.gov.tr, yazmaeserler.diyanet.gov.tr. Consistent with v1.0's TEIS Yesevi 5-witness Cihanşah roster being saturated via Islamisation DB (islam-anatolia.ac.uk). Yusuf Hakîkî Bursavi homonym risk concentrated at Bursa + Bektaşi tekke (Konya Hacı Bektaş BY0000010729 already in v1.0 with disambiguation methodology). The initial Ottoman provincial/Sufi pass was superseded by later chunked direct probes; the remaining gap was a browser certificate-handling pass at yazmalar.gov.tr.
key_findings_by_avenue.do2023_residual_closure: 4 portals (MENA-DOC, HathiTrust, DLME, OPenn) EXHAUSTED-NEGATIVE. Methodological yield: query endpoint discoveries (MENA-DOC backend at hallelit.gbv.de Ha:Lit SPA; DLME Blacklight URL signatures; OPenn = Google site-search relay; HathiTrust UA-/Cloudflare-walled). One new homonym FP class documented: Mughal Shah Jahan (r. 1628-1658) vs Cihanşah Qaraqoyunlu (d. 1467). All 28 DO 2023 article resources now formally closed.

augmentations_no_count_change.content: Pre-1959 institutional history: Az-language popular-history accounts (Az Wikipedia + Azertag.az + Azadliq.info) describe the codex as bequeathed by NYC Armenian collector Arutyun Gazaryan to 'Yerevan University' and discovered there by Lətif Hüseynzadə (Yerevan Pedagogical Institute, not YSU). Discovery 1961; first publication Yerevan 1966. Per Iranica MATENADARAN article, in 1959 the manuscript holdings of multiple Yerevan institutions including YSU were consolidated into Matenadaran. The 'Yerevan University' attribution in popular-history accounts is the pre-1959 institutional location of the codex now held as Matenadaran MS 965. The Az Wiki narrative additionally conflates this provenance with BL Or 9493's separate London examination; these are two different codices.
augmentations_no_count_change.rationale: Adds documented institutional-history context to an existing register entry. Increases scholarly defensibility of the matenadaran_965 entry by clarifying the popular-history-to-institutional-record mapping.

methodological_findings_consolidated: VPN routing affects portal reachability signatures: manuscript.az returned socket-closed under alternate-route, HTTP 200 under direct-route; manuscript.ge returned ECONNREFUSED under alternate-route, REACHABLE_TEST_MODE under direct-route. VPN-routed false-negatives are a documented hazard for Az/Geo/Am portal probing.
Site-restricted Google indexing is a Playwright substitute with a known false-negative class for JS-rendered SPA catalogues; suggestive but not definitive of 'no record exists'.
Parallel probe work should checkpoint findings incrementally so successful search evidence is not lost when final synthesis fails.

Popular-history Azerbaijani-language provenance accounts (Az Wikipedia + Azadliq + Azertag) conflate institutional consolidation events (1959 YSU-Matenadaran transfer) and can manufacture apparent 'multiple witnesses' from a single codex at different institutional moments. Cross-check against Iranica MATENADARAN before treating popular-history MS locations as distinct.

Islamisation DB (islam-anatolia.ac.uk) is the canonical Anatolian Cihanşah witness-discovery surface. Turkish public-facing portals (yazmalar, ISAM, Milli Kütüphane, Diyanet) appear to host the same records under different institutional fronts without adding new Cihanşah witnesses in site-restricted indexing.

Newly-acquired-manuscripts logs on institutional websites are an under-exploited probe surface: AMEA manuscript.az main page acquisition-table directly mentioned 'Jahanshah Hagigi (1405-1467)' obtained from Süleymaniye, providing a direct institutional-self-disclosure of a register-existing entry.

OCR quality as confidence modifier: parallel probe A's distinction between 'strong negative with healthy OCR' (Bankipore Vols II/III/XIII grep quality at 7-8/13 QA hits) and 'degraded OCR residual gap' (Rampur 0-1/14) is the right epistemic posture for printed-catalogue grep-mining.
